topic: Dense automation presentation scheduler and redesign stress harness
currentUserGoal: Keep the ecosystem game fast and smooth even when a 100x100 field has many helpers and effects active at once.
workCompleted: Profiled the actual ecosystem redesign route before optimizing; the measured risk was visual and tween congestion rather than fixed-tick simulation cost.
Added a fixed-size round-robin helper-effect scheduler that batches repeated mechanical pulses into representative presentations.
Kept every automated touch, heal, Run Touch, resource conversion, and field-stage update on the original deterministic production tick.
Set representative presentation gaps to 120 ms on desktop and 210 ms on phone-sized views.
Set per-helper repeat gaps to 620 ms on desktop and 900 ms on phone-sized views so one fast helper cannot monopolize the field.
Added fair helper rotation so all eight helper families remain visible under sustained automation.
Metered automated grass-touch audio using the same adaptive cadence to avoid redundant simultaneous sound starts.
Added a one-click Stress automation playtest control that creates a 100x100 field with 12 copies of every helper and maximum relevant ranks.
Extended the redesign harness with automation rate, cadence, pending pulse payload, representative launches, represented pulses, and visible helper feedback counts.
Added focused scheduler tests for batching, cadence, fairness, repeat limits, phone budgets, requeueing, and reset behavior.
Updated the durable ecosystem design and performance notes with the new presentation contract and measured results.
verificationRun: npm run check passed: ESLint, 216 Vitest tests across 25 files, strict TypeScript, and the Vite production build.
The repeatable stress scenario held 10,000 logical tiles and 100 rendered chunk views without per-frame full-field scans.
A 390x844 browser viewport at about 5,537 automated touches per second showed zero frame spikes and about 0.086 ms average frame work in the sampled window.
An eight-second sustained phone-sized sample kept pending pulse payload between 48 and 71 while presentations continued, rather than accumulating indefinitely.
A 1280x720 sample at about 3,228 automated touches per second showed zero frame spikes, about 0.145 ms average frame work, and 2 ms maximum frame work.
A clean post-build phone stress pass had no browser errors or warnings, zero full-field scans, zero frame spikes, 10 active effects, and 15 active tweens at capture.
A one-sprinkler regression pass kept zero queued pulse backlog, visible field and healing feedback, and immediate automation behavior.
Production deployment dpl_5JHZyDRBe5UrrWqDdh4efjawH1Pc reached READY and grasstouchingsimulator.com served the new scheduler bundle.
knownIssues: The 390x844 measurement changes viewport size but does not emulate a physically slow phone CPU or GPU.
Real-device phone testing remains necessary before claiming a universal hardware FPS floor.
The stress control intentionally mutates playtest save state; Reset prototype restores a clean Run 1 afterward.
The unrelated docs/CODEX_GITHUB_SETUP_GUIDE.md remains untracked and is not part of this slice.
nextRecommendedSteps: Run the deployed stress scenario on one real phone and record frame pacing during ten seconds of dense automation.
Keep later helper-specific effects inside the scheduler instead of adding independent unbounded emitters.
Use the new harness metrics whenever helper animation duration, particle count, or cadence changes.
doNotRevert: Do not delay or discard mechanical helper output to solve presentation load.
Do not launch one visual or sound per automated touch.
Do not replace the fair round-robin scheduler with first-helper-wins scanning.
Do not use the legacy 1,200-tile harness as evidence for ecosystem performance.
Do not include docs/CODEX_GITHUB_SETUP_GUIDE.md without explicit user direction.
